full_judgment:
Mr. Mamnoon Rahman, J:- Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 13-11-1997 (decree drawn on 19-11.-1997) passed by the Subordinate Judge, Second Court Jhalokathi in Title Appeal No.127 of 1994 reversing those dated 27-6-1994 (decree drawn 4-7-1994) passed by the Senior Assistant Judge Kathalia, Jhalkathi in title Suit No.62 of 1993 should not to be set aside and or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The short facts relevant for the disposal for this Rule are that; The opposite party as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.62 of 1993 in Court Assistant Judge, Kathalia, Jhalokathi impleading the petitioner as defendant for declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No.17 of 1991 is null void, void, collusive and not binding upon the opposite party. The plaintiff further prayed for declaration of the title of the property in question as "vested property" described in the schedule of the plaint. 

3. The case of the plaintiff is that the land in question belong Shatish Chandra Roy and S.S record was prepared and published in his name. Shatish Chandra Roy died on 16.7.65 leaving the present petitioner and Mukundra Behare Roy who equal share. Mokunda left for India with his family after the war of 1965 resulting enlistments of his land as vested property. The defendant being only son of Shatish Chandra Roy filed Title Suit No.17 of 1991 challenging the V.P. proceeding and obtained exparte decree. The plaintiff finding no other alternative filed this suit. 

4. The defendant petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegation in the plaint and contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable in its present form. The suit land belong to the father of the petitioner who died on 16.7.1975 leaving the defendant petitioner as the only heirs because the another son Mukunda Behari Roy died in the life time of the predecessor in the interest of the petitioner. The further case of the petitioner defendant is the defendant as plaintiff filed a suit for declaration and the summon was serve property but despite service of summons of that suit the defendants failed to contest resulting exparte decree and as such there is no scope for passing any decree, hence the petitioner defendant prays for dismissal of the suit. 

5. During trial the plaintiffs adduced 4 witnesses while the defendants petitioner adduced 4 witnesses. Both the parties also produced documentary evidence. The Trial Court after hearing the parties and considering the material on record as well as evidence, both oral and documentary dismissed the suit on contest. 

6. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No.175 of 1994 before the District Judge, Jhalkathi. The petitioner defendant being respondent contested the appeal. The said appeal was heard and disposed of by the Subordinate judge; Second Court, Jhalokathi who vide his judgment and decree dated 3.11.1997 and 9.11.1997 allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court. 

7. The petitioner defendant respondent being aggrieved by and dissatisfied by the impugned judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court moved this instant revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure before this
Court and obtained the present rule. 

8. Mr. Md. Harun-or-Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the lower appellate Court committed an error in finding that defendant petitioner obtained exported decree on 14.1:1993 in Title Suit No.17 of 1993 by practicing fraud upon the trial Court which is admittedly beyond the pleadings of plaintiff and such error occasioned failure of Justice. He submits that the Court below misdirected itself in arriving an erroneous finding of fact as well as law and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in such order occasioning failure of Justice. He submits that the V.P. proceeding was initiated in the year 1976 and the ultimate V.P. proceeding vide V.P. No.1 of 1981 was initiated in the year 1981 and such initiation is not permissible in the eye of law as because the Ordinance No.1 of 1969 was repealed with effect from 23.3.1974. By referring the decisions reported in 46 DLR (HCD) 136 and 56 DLR(AD)73 the learned Advocate submits that the Apex Court is of the view that after the natural date of the aforesaid Ordinance no further proceeding for vested property can be initiated and as such the appellate Court below failed to assessed the vital question of law. 

9. Mr. Miaan Sheikh Mohd. Abdullah, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposes the rule. He submits that the petitioner by practicing fraud obtained the exparte decree as because admittedly the brother of the petitioner left for India in the year of 1965. He submits that by suppressing the material facts the petitioner obtained the exparte decree and as such the lower appellate Court has rightly allowed the appeal and set aside the Judgment and decree passed by the trial Court which is a misconceived one. The learned Advocate referred two decisions reported in 27 DLR(AD)52 and 33DLR (AD)30 and submits that despite repeal of the parent law the effect can be continued or enforced. 

10.1 have perused the judgments of both the Court below and the L.C. record. Considering the facts and circumstances, evidence on record the Trial Court found that the petitioner obtained the exparte decree in a rightful manner and accordingly the Trial Court dismissed the suit. The Trial Court also observed there is no scope to allow the prayer of declaration that the property in question is a vested one. While adjudicating the appeal the appellate Court came be a conclusion that the petitioner by practicing fraud obtained the exparte decree and also admittedly the brother of the petitioner was left for India which the plaintiff has been able to proved beyond reasonable doubt by adducing both oral and documentary evidence. 

11. In the instant case it appears that the trial Court dismissed the suit but on an appeal the lower appellate Court allowed the appeal and there by set aside the decree obtained by the petitioner in Title Suit No.17 of 1991 as well as passed a decree of declaration of the land in question as vested property. The main question raised in the instant case is that whether any V.P. proceeding can be initiated or a Civil Court can passed a decree for declaration of a vested property after repeal of the Ordinance I of 1969 on 23.3:1974. 

12. Ordinarily this Court cannot adjudicate any factual aspect even in a case of reversal where there is no misreading or miss-appreciation of evidence by the lower Court, but in .the instant case the vital question of law has been reaised by the petitioner and as such I am of the view that this Court exercising the power under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure has got ample jurisdiction to see or examine the impugned order where there is an allegation of misreading of law. 

13. In the instant case admittedly the V.P proceeding was initiated by opening note sheet in the year 1976 admitted by both the parties in the pleadings. The formal case was initiated in the year 1981 being V.P. case No.4 of 1981. The petitioner came to know about the said proceeding and filed the .suit for declaration resulting obtainment of exparte decree. On perusal of the L.C. record it appears that the plaintiffs admitted the receipt of the summons of that suit but due to the fault of the officers the plaintiff cannot contest the suit. In the above circumstances it cannot be said that the plaintiff is not aware of the said suit. Also the plaintiff failed to show any positive case practice of fraud or collusion. 

14. In the instant case 'the entire V.P. proceeding was initiated after 23.3.1974 i.e. the date on which the Ordinance 1 of 1969 was repealed. Whether such proceeding can he initiated after such repeal came before this Court wherein the High Court Division in the case of Laxmi Kanta Roy Vs. Upazilla Nirbahi Officer and another reported in. 46 DLR 136 held; 
"At the very outset it has drawn my attention in this case as to whether the institution of the V.P. cases No.142 of 1980 was maintainable in the eye of law. The Defence of Pakistan ordinace and Rules came in the year 1965 the Defence of Pakistan ordinance and Rules were repealed in the year 1969 but by ordinance No.1 of 1969 promulgated by the then Central Government or Pakistan, some of the provisions of the Defence of Pakistan Rules were kept alive and continued. Thereafter by Act No.XLV of 1974 the Ordinance No.1 of 1969 was repeated on 23.3.74. After the repeat of Ordinance No.1 of 1969 whether any proceeding unde the said ordinance and Rule could be started. Admittedly, the present Vested Property case was started in the year 1980. Unfortunately, this point was neither raised by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff nor the learned Judges had taken notice of the law which was repealed in the year 1974. This point was not specifically agitated and. no issue was framed on it. Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that since it is a question of law it can be agitated in this Court at this provisional stage. In this case Mr. Quayum has referred to the case of Nittay Gopal Roy Barman Vs. Pran Gopal Nandi and others, 32 DLR 11. In the aforesaid Judgment it is categorically held by his Lordship that after repeal of the Ordinance No.1 of 1969 by Act No. XLV of .1971 on 23.3.74 the authority was not completed to start such vested property proceeding in the eye of law in the aforesaid judgment his Lordship held as follows; 
"Mere claim of the Assistant Custodian that the property of the deceased leslator is an enemy property in respect of which an enemy property case was started in 1974 in not sufficient for coming to a conclusion that the property is an enemy property" 
I fully agree with the view of his Lordship expressed in the aforesaid decision. Since the law on Enemy Property itself died with the repeal of Ordinance 1 of 1969 on 23.3.74 by Act XLV of 1974, no further vested property case can be started thereafter on the basis of the law which is already dead. So I find that the starting of the vested property case No.142 of 1980 in the year 1980 is absolutely without jurisdiction and has no legal basis at all" 

15. The same question has been raised before their Lordships of our Appellate Division and their Lordships in the case of Aroti Rani Paul Vs. Sudarshan Komar Paul and another reported in 56 DLR(AD) 73 held; 
"We have perused the judgments of the Court below as well as the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. It appears that both the Courts below having considered the oral and documentary evidence, concurrently held that the transfer by registered deeds of 1975 vide Exhibits-5 and 6 as made by father and uncle living in a joint undivided Hindu family under the Dayabhag School of law, is valid. Since the father and uncle being in Bangladesh in the year 1957, transferred the suit property, by the aforesaid registered deeds of gift, cannot be declared an enemy property in view of the aforesaid decision as referred to above in 46DLR 136 any we accepted the argument of Mr. Bhuiyan that since the law of enemy property itself died with file repeal of Ordinance No.91of 1969 on 23.3.1974 no further Vested Property case can be started thereafter on the basis Of the law which is already dead." 

16. On perusal of the same it appears that their Lordships in a clear language held that after the death of the Ordinance No.1 of 1969 with effect from 23.3.1974 there can be no proceeding relates to vested property. 

17. I have perused the decisions as referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite party. Admittedly as per the said decisions even after repeal of the Emergency Ordinance, 1965 a new Ordinance came namely Ordinance No.1 of 1969 and in the said Ordinance there is a clause that notwithstanding dissolution of the Emergency Ordinance of 1965 some provisions annexed in the said Ordinance of 1965 shall remain enforce under the Ordinance of 1969. But the learned Advocate failed to show us any such clause in the law by which the Ordinance 1 of 1969 was repealed. 

18. In view of the Judgment passed by our Apex Court, I am of the view that any proceeding by way of V.P. case or suit in a Civil Court so far it relates to declaration of any property as vested property is learned after 23.3.1974 i.e after repeal of the Ordinance 1 of 1969. In the instant case in hand admittedly the V.P. proceeding was initiated after the aforesaid date and as such the decree of declaration that the property in question is vested property passed by the lower Appellate Court is not sustainable in the eye of law. Furthermore, the plaintiff also miserably failed to proved that the defendant obtained the exparte decree by practicing fraud and collusively. Rather admittedly the same was passed within the knowledge of the plaintiff of the instant suit. 

19. Considering the facts and circumstances and the provision of law and the decisions as referred to I find substance in this Rule. Accordingly the Rule is made atisc2lute. The impugned judgment and decree passed by the Lower Appellate Court dated 3.11.1997 is hereby set aside. The judgment and decree passed by the trial Court is affirmed. 

20. Send down the L.C. record with a copy of this judgment at once.

End.
